question: Why does American Express report provisions for credit losses when Visa does not?
expected_answer: American Express is a closed-loop network that issues its own cards and holds card member loans and receivables on its balance sheet, so under CECL it must reserve for expected credit losses. Visa is an open-loop network that only moves money between issuers and acquirers and does not lend, so it carries no consumer credit risk and reports no such provisions.
